requirement: Return the k highest scoring entries from any iterable in descending order using memory bounded by k, preferring earlier entries when scores tie, and rejecting a negative k.
skeleton: Frozen Entry dataclass and a top_k function keeping a min-heap of (score, negative index, entry) tuples of size k.
caption: Top-k selection over a stream of scored entries with the standard-library heapq module. Entry is a frozen, slotted dataclass holding a name and a score. top_k(entries, k) raises ValueError saying k must not be negative when k is below zero and returns an empty list when k is zero. Otherwise it walks the entries with enumerate and builds a key tuple of the score, the negated position and the entry, so that among equal scores an earlier entry compares larger and the entry itself is never compared. While the heap holds fewer than k tuples it pushes with heapq.heappush; after that it replaces the smallest tuple with heapq.heapreplace only when the new tuple is strictly larger than heap[0]. Memory therefore stays bounded by k even for a generator. The result is the heap sorted in reverse, reduced to the entries, so the highest score comes first and ties appear in input order. The fixture asserts that the top two of scores 3, 5, 1 and 4 are b then d, that among three entries tied at 2 the first two win, that asking for more entries than exist returns all of them in descending order, that a generator of ten entries yields 9, 8 and 7, that k of zero returns an empty list, and that a negative k raises ValueError.

plan.intent: Pick the best k entries from a stream
constraints: The result is sorted from the highest score down
A k of zero returns an empty list and a negative k raises ValueError

rationale.teaches: A size-bounded min-heap of key tuples, with a negated index as the tie-breaker so payloads are never compared.
rationale.why: Top-k helpers usually get the replacement comparison, the heap size or the tie order subtly wrong, and those errors only show on inputs with ties or with more candidates than slots.

ops.docstring: Select the top scoring entries with a bounded heap and stable tie-breaking.

candidates.why_wrong: A negative k falls through to an index error on the empty heap instead of a ValueError.
The heap replaces its minimum with smaller items, so it keeps the lowest scores after the first k.
The heap is sorted ascending, so the result starts with the lowest of the selected scores.
The heap is allowed to grow to k plus one entries, so one extra entry is returned.
The raw index is used as the tie-breaker, so later entries win ties.
